questions.question: A spherical gas bubble of radius r expands such that its surface area increases at a constant rate of $8\pi\text{ cm}^2/\text{s}$. When the radius of the bubble is $2\text{ cm}$, the rate of increase of its volume is:
If energy $E$, velocity $v$, and force $F$ are chosen as fundamental quantities, the dimensional formula of mass density $\rho$ is:

A particle starts from rest from the origin and moves along the $x$-axis with an acceleration given by $a(t) = (6t - 4)\text{ m/s}^2$ (where $t$ is in seconds). The displacement of the particle between $t = 1\text{ s}$ and $t = 3\text{ s}$ is:
Two vectors are given by $\vec{A} = 2\hat{i} + 3\hat{j} - \hat{k}$ and $\vec{B} = -\hat{i} + 2\hat{j} + 4\hat{k}$. The scalar projection of vector $(\vec{A} + \vec{B})$ onto vector $\vec{A}$ is:

A screw gauge has a pitch of $0.5\text{ mm}$ and $50$ divisions on its circular scale. When the jaws are brought in contact without any object, the $45\text{th}$ division of the circular scale coincides with the reference line (the zero of the circular scale lies above the reference line). While measuring the diameter of a small metal sphere, the main scale reading is $3.0\text{ mm}$ and the $25\text{th}$ circular scale division coincides with the reference line. The true diameter of the sphere is:
The maximum and minimum values of the function $f(\theta) = 5\sin\theta + 12\cos\theta - 3$ are respectively:

A small ball is released from rest from the top of a multi-storey building of height $H$. It traverses a distance equal to $\frac{7}{16}H$ during the last second of its free fall. Taking $g = 10\text{ m/s}^2$, the height $H$ of the building is:

A particle is projected from the ground in the $x$-$y$ vertical plane such that its trajectory is described by $y = \sqrt{3}x - \frac{g}{20}x^2$, where $x$ and $y$ are in meters and $g = 10\text{ m/s}^2$. The horizontal range $R$ and maximum height $H$ reached by the projectile are:

A river $400\text{ m}$ wide is flowing due east at a uniform speed of $3\text{ m/s}$. A motorboat that can travel at $5\text{ m/s}$ in still water sets out from the south bank. To reach the point directly opposite on the north bank, at what angle to the direction of river flow should the boat be steered, and how much time will it take to cross?

A particle moves in a straight line along the positive $x$-axis such that its velocity depends on position as $v = 4\sqrt{x}$ (in SI units). If the particle was at $x = 0$ at time $t = 0$, its average velocity over the time interval from $t = 0$ to $t = 3\text{ s}$ is:
The area enclosed by the curve $y = 2e^{2x}$, the $x$-axis, and the vertical lines $x = 0$ and $x = \ln 2$ is:

Three vectors satisfy $\vec{A} + \vec{B} + \vec{C} = \vec{0}$. Their magnitudes are $|\vec{A}| = 5$, $|\vec{B}| = 12$, and $|\vec{C}| = 13$. The magnitude of the cross product $|\vec{A} \times \vec{B}|$ and the angle $\phi$ between $\vec{A}$ and $\vec{C}$ are:

A projectile is fired from the ground with an initial speed $u = 20\sqrt{3}\text{ m/s}$ at an angle of $60^\circ$ above the horizontal. Neglecting air resistance, the time after launch at which its velocity vector becomes perpendicular to its initial velocity vector is: ($g = 10\text{ m/s}^2$)
options: The velocity vector will never become perpendicular to the initial velocity

questions.question: Two particles $A$ and $B$ are projected simultaneously in the same vertical plane. Particle $A$ is projected from ground level with speed $u_A = 40\text{ m/s}$ at an angle of $30^\circ$ above the horizontal. Particle $B$ is projected horizontally from a tower of height $h = 20\text{ m}$ directly facing $A$ with a horizontal speed $v_B = 10\text{ m/s}$. If the two particles collide in mid-air, the initial horizontal separation $d$ between their launch points must be: ($g = 10\text{ m/s}^2$)

Rain is falling at an inclined angle with the vertical. A man walking horizontally due east at $2\text{ m/s}$ observes the rain to be falling vertically downwards. When he increases his speed to $4\text{ m/s}$ in the same direction, the rain appears to strike him at an angle of $45^\circ$ with the vertical. The true speed of rain relative to the ground is:

A particle moves along a straight line. The graph between the square of its velocity ($v^2$) and its position ($x$) is a straight line as shown below. The acceleration of the particle and the time taken by it to travel from $x = 0$ to $x = 8\text{ m}$ are respectively:
The percentage errors in the measurement of $a, b, c$, and $d$ are $1.5\%$, $2.0\%$, $1.0\%$, and $4.0\%$ respectively. The maximum percentage error in the calculation of $Z$ $=a2b3/2c3d$ is:

Two cars $P$ and $Q$ move in the same direction along a straight single-lane road. Car $P$ moves at a constant speed of $25\text{ m/s}$, while car $Q$, which is $50\text{ m}$ ahead of $P$, travels at a constant speed of $15\text{ m/s}$. The driver of car $P$ applies the brakes, producing a constant deceleration $a$. The limiting value of $a$ required to avoid a collision is:

A ball is thrown from the top of a $40\text{ m}$ high cliff with an initial speed of $20\text{ m/s}$ at an angle of $30^\circ$ above the horizontal. Taking $g = 10\text{ m/s}^2$, the total time of flight of the ball and the horizontal distance from the base of the cliff to where it strikes the ground are:

Two stones are projected from the ground with the same initial speed $u$ at complementary angles of projection $\theta$ and $(90^\circ - \theta)$. They attain maximum heights of $H_1 = 45\text{ m}$ and $H_2 = 20\text{ m}$ respectively. The common horizontal range $R$ of the two stones is:

A projectile is fired from the ground with speed $u = 20\text{ m/s}$ at an angle of $45^\circ$ to the horizontal. Taking $g = 10\text{ m/s}^2$, the radius of curvature of its trajectory at the highest point is:
A force vector $\vec{F}$ of magnitude $12\sqrt{3}\text{ N}$ makes equal acute angles with the positive $x$, $y$, and $z$ coordinate axes. The Cartesian vector form of $\vec{F}$ is:

Assertion (A): The measured values $2.30\text{ cm}$ and $0.0230\text{ m}$ both possess exactly three significant figures.

Reason (R): A change of units shifts the position of the decimal point but does not alter the number of significant figures in a measured quantity.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A).

questions.question: The graph shows position as a function of time for two trains running on parallel tracks. Which one of the following statements is true?
options: At time $t_B$, both trains have the same velocity
Both trains have the same velocity at some time after $t_B$
Both trains have the same velocity at some time before $t_B$
Somewhere on the graph, both trains have the same acceleration

questions.question: The velocity-time graph of body is shown in figure. Which of the following statements is wrong?
options: Ratio of average velocities for times $OA$ and $AB = 1$
Magnitude of average accelerations for times $OA$ and $OB$ is in inverse of ratio of distances covered
Ratio of distance covered for times $OA$ and $AB$ is $1 : 3$

questions.question: Twelve persons are initially at the twelve corners of a regular polygon of twelve sides of side $a$. Each person now moves with a uniform speed $v$ in such a manner that 1 is always directed towards 2, 2 towards 3, 3 towards 4, and so on. The time after which they meet is:

A river of width $400\text{ m}$ flows with a constant speed of $5\text{ m/s}$. A swimmer who can swim at a speed of $4\text{ m/s}$ in still water dives into the river to cross it. To minimize his downstream drift, at what angle to the upstream direction must he swim, and what will be his minimum drift?

A stunt motorcyclist attempts to jump horizontally across a canal of width $7.2\text{ m}$. The take-off ledge is $1.8\text{ m}$ higher than the landing bank on the opposite side. Assuming horizontal take-off and neglecting air resistance, the minimum horizontal speed required to safely clear the canal is: (Take $g = 10\text{ m/s}^2$)

A particle is moving along the x axis. Its position ($x$) with time ($t$) is given by $x = 3t^2 - \frac{t^3}{2}$, where $x$ is in metre and $t$ for the interval 0 $\le$ t $\le$ 4s is in second. Match the condition of list-I with time interval and instant of list-II.

List-I List-II
(A) Velocity and acceleration will be in the same direction (I) At $t = 0$ and $t = 4\text{ s}$ 
(B) Particle is at origin (II) $0 < t < 2\text{ s}$
(C) Particle is retarding (III) At $t = 0$ and $t = 6\text{ s}$
(D) speed is zero (IV) $2\text{ s} < t < 4\text{ s}$

Two electric trains $A$ and $B$ are moving directly towards each other on a straight track with constant speeds of $54\text{ km h}^{-1}$ and $36\text{ km h}^{-1}$ respectively. When the distance between them is $45\text{ km}$, a surveillance drone takes off from train $A$ and flies along the track directly towards train $B$ at a constant speed of $72\text{ km h}^{-1}$. The instant it reaches train $B$, it turns around and flies back towards train $A$, repeating this back-and-forth journey until the two trains meet. The total distance covered by the drone before the trains meet is:

In a hypothetical but dimensionally consistent physical equation, the electrical permittivity of a medium ($\varepsilon$) is given by:

$\varepsilon = \alpha\sqrt{W} + \beta x^3$

where $W$ represents work done and $x$ represents position. The dimensional formula of the ratio $\left(\frac{\alpha}{\beta}\right)$ is:

A massive wheel in a space simulation facility rotates about a fixed central axis at a constant angular speed $\omega_0$. An astronaut in training, seated in a capsule at the outer rim at a distance $R_1$ from the axis, rotates along with an instrument payload placed closer to the hub at a distance $R_2$ (where $R_1 > R_2$).

If both the capsule and the payload undergo steady circular motion together, which of the following correctly compares their angular speeds ($\omega$), tangential speeds ($v$), and magnitudes of centripetal acceleration ($a_c$)?

Consider the following real-world physical situations:

  • Case A: A hockey puck sliding freely in varying directions across a flat, horizontal sheet of ice.
  • Case B: A weather balloon drifting and ascending through turbulent layers of the atmosphere.
  • Case C: A marker dot painted at the edge of a spinning ceiling fan blade.

Which of the following cases represent two-dimensional motion (motion in a plane)?
options: Case A and Case C only
Case B and Case C only
Case A, Case B, and Case C

What is the ratio of the magnitude of the satellite's average velocity to its average speed over this interval?

The velocity of the particle at $x = 8\text{ m}$ is:

is:

The equilibrium constant ($K_p$) of the reaction increases.
